message.content:
**Most Famous American Composers (by influence and recognition)**  

| Composer | Lifespan | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|----------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** | 1898–1937 | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, *Porgy & Bess* |
| **Aaron Copland** | 1900–1990 | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man*, *Rodeo* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** | 1918–1990 | *West Side Story*, *On the Town*, *Candide* (composer/arranger) |
| **John Williams** | 1932– | *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park* (film scores) |
| **Philip Glass** | 1937– | Minimalist works: *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks*, *Koyaanisqatsi* |
| **Samuel Barber** | 1910–1981 | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* |
| **Charles Ives** | 1874–1954 | *The Unanswered Question*, *Concord Sonata* |
| **John Philip Sousa** | 1854–1932 | “The Stars and Stripes Forever”, “The Washington Post” |
| **Stephen Foster** | 1826–1864 | “Oh! Susanna”, “Camptown Races” (American folk/popular music) |
| **George Frideric Handel** (American-born in Germany, but his *Messiah* was first performed in the US) | 1685–1759 | *Messiah* (first performed in Philadelphia, 1742) |

These composers are widely recognized for shaping American music across genres—from classical and opera to film scores and popular music.
